packet.comment: Begin packet at either accepted lowercase header, retaining the boundary required only by packet. packet.md#detection: Detection alone does not accept `packetx`, `packet2`, or `packet-BETA`. packet.md#header-boundaries-and-gaps: Only `packet` requires immediate common whitespace, `%%` or end of text. packet.md#header-boundaries-and-gaps: `packet-beta` has no such check and may touch a block or common form. common.md#leading-whitespace: Whitespace, line terminators, directives, and comment regions before the first unit of the diagram's lexer are trivia and are not seen by the diagram's grammar.

patterns.comment: Reuse hidden YAML before the range-dash rule. packet.md#ordered-rules: The range dash has an explicit longer alternative: choose a whole hidden YAML match instead when one starts there. packet.md#hidden-forms: At any unit start, hidden YAML starts with `---`, zero or more ASCII spaces/tabs and LF, even off a physical line start.

Reuse the native hidden directive form. packet.md#hidden-forms: After optional ASCII padding, native hidden DIRECTIVE starts with `%%{` and takes as few arbitrary characters as possible through `}%%` followed by LF, common whitespace or EOF.
Reuse native percent comments. packet.md#comments-and-common-trivia: Native comments read optional ASCII indentation, `%%` and maximal content before physical LF/CR; LS/PS remain content.

Reuse the common title and accessibility forms. packet.md#composite-common-forms: Optional ASCII indentation may precede each common form. `title-line` is `title` alone or followed by one ASCII space/tab and possibly empty line text. `acc-title-line` is `accTitle`, zero or more ASCII spaces/tabs, colon and possibly empty line text; `acc-descr-line` uses `accDescr`. packet.md#composite-common-forms: `acc-descr-block` is `accDescr`, zero or more common whitespace characters, `{`, and arbitrary text through the first required `}`.

Read an unsigned integer and check its following boundary through directives. packet.md#numbers-and-strings: An integer is `0`, or a nonzero ASCII digit followed by as many ASCII digits as possible while the next character is not a dot. The zero alternative ends after one digit. common.md#a-directive-is-a-token-boundary: A directive is trivia and not diagram text.
patterns.name: constant.numeric.mermaid

patterns.comment: Reuse quoted strings with backslash escapes. packet.md#numbers-and-strings: A string starts with either quote and requires the same closing quote. It contains zero or more ordinary characters other than that quote/backslash, or a backslash and one character other than LF, CR, LS or PS; take as many complete components as possible.

Read the range and relative operators and the label separator. packet.md#grammar: A missing endpoint, colon or quoted label rejects, as do adjacent same-line blocks or a common statement after a completed block.
